properties.description:
BUILT 2026-08-21 on Anthony's word, promoting option (a) of dec:idea-a-gap-can-be-scheduled-into-an-increment-like-any-other-work. DISTINCT FROM that Decision, which records the four options and stays as the reasoning; this is the one that was taken.

HIS WORDS, 2026-08-20: "add gaps that need to be closed to increments/epochs." The design carried 89 open gaps, 85 never put to anybody — a list that endures and is skimmed is durable and useless at the same time. Scheduling is what turns a standing list into work with a moment attached.

⭐ IT SCHEDULES THE QUESTION, NOT THE GAP, and that is the whole design. A GAP IS NOT A NODE: gaps are recomputed from the condition on every run, which is why one carried the same id all day and why it vanishes when the condition is actually fixed rather than needing closing by hand. That property is worth keeping, and it means there is nothing to hang a schedule on. But gap_to_prompt already mints a durable question:<id> the moment a gap is put to somebody, and open_questions already tracks it until answered. The durable node already existed; only the edge did not. SCHEDULED_FOR now accepts Question alongside Requirement and Capability.

⭐ DELIVERY IS ANSWERING, and nothing could stand in for it. There is no artifact to look for and no check to run — the whole content of closing a gap is that the person whose judgement it needed gave one. answer_question is the only thing that sets it, so delivery stays COMPUTED rather than asserted, exactly like every other scheduled item.

🛑 A WITHDRAWN QUESTION REPORTS `discontinued`, NOT `outstanding`, and this was added beyond the plan. `outstanding` means "nobody has said whether this was deferred or discontinued". Somebody said. Letting it fall through would put the question again on every run about something already taken off the table — the identical false reading fixed hours earlier in fact:a-capability-delivered-as-a-model-change-can-never-be-reported-delivered, shipping on day one of a brand-new mechanism.

⚠️ STATED LIMIT, and it is a real one. Delivered means THE QUESTION WAS ANSWERED. It does NOT mean the answer was written back into the design — that is separate work, and the loop already counts it separately as `unwritten_answers`. A scheduled question can therefore read `delivered` while the gap it came from is still open, because the gap closes when the DESIGN changes and the question closes when the PERSON speaks. Those are two different acts and the schedule tracks the second.

⚠️ NOT DEMONSTRATED ON LIVE DATA, said rather than left to be assumed. This graph holds exactly ONE Question and it is already answered, so there is no natural outstanding-to-delivered transition to show here. The six tests cover the behaviour; manufacturing a live schedule that did not fit the data would have been theatre.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKED, and why it could not have shipped yesterday: closing a gap is almost always MODEL work rather than a file. Before Capability.delivery existed, every scheduled question would have inherited the artifact-required blindness and sat `outstanding` forever. The Decision said these two had to be answered together or delivery first — delivery was first.
properties.name: The resolution of a gap can be scheduled into an increment — by scheduling the Question it became
